nodes.name: Long-reach EML/DFB laser diodes (1310nm for coherent modules)
nodes.description: Externally-modulated laser (EML) and distributed-feedback (DFB) laser diodes operating at 1310nm wavelength, used in coherent optical transceivers for long-reach datacenter interconnect (10+ km), especially in new high-capacity modules (800G+, 1.6T coherent). These differ fundamentally from short-reach 850nm VCSELs: they enable longer reach with constrained manufacturing capacity concentrated among 4–5 vendors globally. Capacity constraints documented in 2024–2025; suppliers expanding capacity through 2026–2027.

metrics.name: EML/DFB laser wavelength (coherent datacom standard)
metrics.description: 1310nm is the standard C-band window for coherent optical transceivers in long-reach datacenter applications per ITU-T and OIF specifications.

metrics.name: Global EML/DFB laser supplier concentration (top-3 share)
metrics.description: Top 3 suppliers (Coherent/Lumentum/Mitsubishi) control approximately 70–75% of datacom EML/DFB output per Yole and SemiAnalysis analyst reports; constrained by epitaxial-fab capacity.

metrics.name: InP substrate demand for EML/DFB production
metrics.description: InP laser-diode supply is constrained by upstream InP substrate availability. Coherent CEO stated (2026 Q1) that InP capacity is constrained and will double over the next 12 months.

metrics.name: EML/DFB laser capacity expansion lead time
metrics.description: Adding capacity for EML/DFB lasers requires dedicated epitaxial-growth tools, waveguide processing, and packaging qualification; typical expansion lead time 18–24 months.

nodes.notes: EML/DFB lasers are a separate supply chain from VCSEL arrays. The 2024–2025 optical transceiver supply tightness was partly driven by constrained EML capacity as demand shifted toward coherent (long-reach) module designs. Current constraint is upstream at the InP substrate and epitaxy layers rather than finished-device packaging. If long-reach transceiver demand doubles, EML laser supply becomes critical path.

nodes.name: Specialty compound semiconductor foundry (InP/GaAs device fabrication and packaging)
nodes.description: Post-epitaxy processing to complete laser diode and photodiode devices: optical waveguide definition (stripe geometry etch, ridge waveguide), quantum-well layer tuning, contact metallization, facet preparation (cleaving, coating), and hermetic packaging (TO-46 cans, butterfly packages, or integrated module packages). Process steps differ sharply from silicon: ridge etch precision (±50 nm), facet antireflection coatings (specific wavelengths), and packaging reliability (10+ year MTTF at 125°C). Supply base is concentrated: EML/DFB devices made by ~5 suppliers (Coherent, Lumentum, Mitsubishi Electric, Sumitomo Electric, Broadcom); VCSEL fabrication by 6–8 vendors (Broadcom, Coherent, Lumentum, HLJ, VPEC, Vertilite). Device fabrication capacity expansion requires 12–18 months per fab line (equipment procurement + installation + qualification).

metrics.name: EML/DFB laser device suppliers (global)
metrics.description: Worldwide EML/DFB laser device manufacturers at commercial scale for 1310nm coherent datacom: Coherent, Lumentum, Mitsubishi Electric, Sumitomo Electric, Broadcom (emerging). Oligopoly concentration (top 3 = ~70–75% share per Yole/SemiAnalysis).

metrics.name: VCSEL device suppliers (global, 850nm+ datacom-class)
metrics.description: VCSEL device manufacturers with commercial datacenter production: Broadcom, Coherent, Lumentum, HLJ Technology (Taiwan), VPEC (Taiwan), Vertilite (China), Philips Lumileds (private), and emerging regional suppliers. Top 3 dominate ~65–70% share.

metrics.name: Specialty compound fab line expansion lead time
metrics.description: Adding new InP/GaAs device fabrication line: equipment procurement (3–4 mo), installation (2–3 mo), recipe qualification and yield ramp (6–8 mo). Total: 12–18 months.

nodes.notes: Post-epitaxy fabrication is a critical but secondary bottleneck: capacity constraints are more severe upstream (InP substrate and epitaxy layers) but specialized equipment (ridge-etch tools, facet-coating systems) and process recipes create vendor lock-in. EML constraint is attributed to: (1) limited InP epitaxy capacity feeding device fabs, (2) specialized device fab lines with long setup times, and (3) capacity pre-allocation by tier-1 customers. VCSEL is less constrained than EML overall, but specific form factors (high-density arrays for 800G+) face short-term capacity gaps. Hyperscaler prepayments and long-term capacity contracts (e.g., NVIDIA $2B Lumentum investment March 2026, $2B Coherent investment) are separate capacity-lock events and are not modeled in this node.

evidence.title: Coherent CEO: InP laser capacity constrained, doubling over next 12 months (2026 Q1)
evidence.summary: Coherent Corporation CEO statement on InP laser capacity status: current capacity is constrained; company plans to double capacity within 12 months through upgraded epitaxial-growth facilities and process optimization.
evidence.excerpt: InP laser capacity is currently constrained. We plan to double our capacity over the next 12 months through process improvements and equipment expansion.

evidence.title: EML/DFB laser supplier market concentration: Coherent, Lumentum, Mitsubishi Electric top 3 (2024–2025)
evidence.summary: Yole Développement analyst report on optical transceivers for datacenters: top 3 EML/DFB laser suppliers (Coherent, Lumentum, Mitsubishi Electric) command 70–75% of the datacom market. Capacity constraints limit growth.
evidence.excerpt: Top 3 suppliers control approximately 70–75% of the EML/DFB laser market for coherent datacom modules. Supply remains capacity-constrained through 2026.
